mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weekly means (-72.0 to -64.6), indicating an ongoing recovery in discretionary mobility. This momentum is expected to persist and push the 4-week mean further upward.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -72.0 at t-2w to -64.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite the three-week rising streak, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in TRANSIT of more than 5 points signals renewed commuting and errand travel, which mechanically feeds into increased retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -64.3 at t-2w to -59.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC's subsequent 2-week mean does not increase relative to the prior 2 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates restored commuting routines that compound: workers traveling to offices generate both transit demand and adjacent retail/recreation stops, producing a stronger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -54.6 to -53.1 and TRANSIT rose from -64.3 to -59.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise for two consecutive weeks but the subsequent 4-week RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A declining RESIDENTIAL index (from 20.0 to 17.4 over the last two weeks) reflects loosening stay-at-home policy pressure under Lombardy's tiered zone system, which should translate into increased out-of-home retail and recreation activity over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.0 at t-2w to 17.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 2-week mean, the policy-easing mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The rebound in PARKS mobility (from -63.7 to -58.7 over the last two weeks) reflects improving late-winter weather in Lombardy, which encourages outdoor activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -63.7 at t-2w to -58.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising through February but RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean fails to increase, the seasonal spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized in a narrow band (-39.4 to -31.4) over the last three weeks, suggesting households have settled into a routine shopping pattern rather than precautionary stockpiling, freeing discretionary trips that raise RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within a 10-point band for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged between -39.4 and -31.4 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not increase relative to the current week, the behavioral stabilization hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES crosses above -50 (a threshold historically associated with relaxed zone restrictions in Lombardy), office reopening accelerates and drives a corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks due to lunchtime and after-work retail trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -54.6 to -53.1, approaching the -50 threshold
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses above -50 but RETAIL_REC's 2-week mean does not rise relative to the prior 2 weeks, the threshold policy hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL and rise in TRANSIT within the same week signals households shifting from home-confinement behavior to active errand-running, producing a compounded short-term boost to RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 17.4 and TRANSIT rose to -59.1 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises together but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not increase, the interaction-driven behavioral hypothesis is rejected.
